purpose: Append-only log of PROVEN map layer order / paint corrections. Owner mandate 2026-08-16: 'setup proper ordering logs when we prove a correction ... we need this to always work'. A correction that is not in this log does not exist. Every entry carries a machine-checkable invariant that a test enforces, so a proven fix cannot silently regress.
rules: APPEND ONLY. Never edit or delete a past entry. To overturn one, add a new entry and set the old entry's `refuted_by` to the new id.

An entry may only be added after a PAIRED experiment: the symptom must be shown PRESENT with the lever in its stock state and ABSENT with one single variable changed, at every zoom in the ladder. A one-way observation is not proof.
Every entry MUST name an `invariant` that a test asserts, and `enforced_by` MUST point at that test. An entry with no enforcement is a story, not a proof.
Verify the lever TOOK EFFECT before reading its result. A silently reverted lever reports 'no effect' identically to one that has none (see LOP-0001 `traps`).
Single-zoom results are inadmissible for any zoom-interpolated property. Run the ladder.

entries.title: The marine coastal halo is `ocean-mask-buffer`; it must be OFF by default
entries.symptom: A dark band hugging every coastline between the land and the marine field, plus faceted dark blobs over coastal land at Cape Canaveral / Merritt Island. Worse when zooming out; absent at close zoom.

painter.line_opacity: 1.0 until z8.5, ramping to 0.0 by z9.5

entries.mechanism: The buffer paints near-black while the basemap water it was designed to blend into composites to a MEDIUM SLATE (`water` fill hsl(197,15%,43%) at opacity 0.25 over the `land` background hsl(214,17%,31%)). It therefore darkens whatever it sits above. On a convoluted coastline a 60px stroke with round joins self-overlaps, and at 0.9 alpha the overlaps compound into faceted dark polygons over land. The `line-opacity` ramp is the ONLY thing that makes close zoom look clean.

experiment.method: paired A/B at a fixed scene, one variable, order toggled in place, re-verified after settle at every stop

legs.change: full opacity, layer moved BELOW webgl-marine-particles
legs.halo: band ABSENT over water, but darkening APPEARS OVER COASTAL LAND - REJECTED as the fix

zoom_ladder.stock: halo SEVERE - whole Gulf, Atlantic seaboard, Cuba, Hispaniola, Central America
faceted dark blobs over Cape Canaveral / Merritt Island

experiment.coverage_independence: The halo appeared in every opaque regime, so the defect is independent of the coverage state machine.

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: stack order - move the buffer below the marine field
rejected_hypotheses.why_rejected: clears the band over water but lands the near-black line above ocean-mask-fill, darkening coastal land. The symptom moves rather than clearing. Owner caught this.
it made an ordering relationship deterministic, but the halo reproduces with the planner ON and vanishes with the buffer's opacity alone at the stock order. Real bug, wrong bug.
measured ENGAGED AND CORRECT in the very frames showing the halo; does not govern a style layer
washOverlayMode replace:false throughout; does not govern a style layer

traps.detail: OceanMask.js re-asserts visibility on every sync tick while a marine layer is active. Measured: set to 'none', read back 'visible' 2.5s later. This leg would have shown no pixel change and CLEARED the actual culprit.
Every buffer property is zoom-interpolated. A close-zoom check passes because line-opacity ramps to 0 above z9.5, not because the defect is absent.
webgl-marine-particles is a custom layer and does not appear in getStyle().layers. Read map.style._order for the true order.

fix.change: `bufferOn` no longer defaults to true whenever a marine layer is active; ocean-mask-buffer is now OPT-IN only via window.__RAW_WATER_TEMP_COAST_BUFFER__ === true

invariant.statement: ocean-mask-buffer must not be enabled merely because a marine layer is active. Its enablement must depend ONLY on the explicit __RAW_WATER_TEMP_COAST_BUFFER__ opt-in.
invariant.checkable: resolveCoastBufferOn(activeMarineLayer, flag) === flag, for every activeMarineLayer value
